Subject: Embeddings cutover for ACME - timeline & sample set

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're starting to pin down dates for the embedding + rerank migration and wanted to surface a few constraints from our side and get your recommendation on approach. Quick context: ACME search indexes ~500k docs (mixed long/short), typical query P95 latency target is 120ms, and we want minimal search downtime for the public site.

Key asks:
- What's the recommended backfill strategy for our dataset size (bulk reindex vs incremental seed + live catch-up)?
- If we use a vector DB, which vendors do you recommend for this workload (Pinecone, Milvus, self-hosted FAISS) and what tradeoffs should we expect?
- How should we structure rerank evals to surface regressions early?

We have a tentative maintenance window May 22-23 but can be flexible if needed. Attached is a small sample manifest (sample_manifest.csv) and a short report with query distributions. Can we get a runbook/plan from Redwood that spells out the timeline, owners, and rollback criteria?

Thanks,
Jia

Subject: Re: Embeddings cutover for ACME - timeline & sample set

Hi Jia —

Appreciate the context and the sample. We'll put together a concise runbook that covers the options and a recommended schedule. High-level guidance up front:

1) Two sensible patterns for your size:
   - Bulk backfill (fast, simpler correctness model): create a fresh vector index and bulk push all vectors during an offline window. Pros: single consistent index, predictable latency for bulk push. Cons: requires switch-over and double-write or short redirect period.
   - Seed + incremental catch-up (low-impact, continuous): seed the index with high-volume segments first and then incrementally catch up new/changed docs while keeping the old index live. Pros: minimal downtime, easier to rollback. Cons: requires careful idempotency and reconciliation.

2) Vector DB choices:
   - Pinecone: managed, good latency SLAs, easier ops for ACME.
   - Milvus (self-managed/multi-node): more control, better for heavy custom sharding, but ops burden.
   - FAISS (self-hosted): lower cost at scale but you take on sharding/replication.

3) Rerank evals:
   - We'll propose a 1,000-query evaluation set (stratified by query type and doc length), run baselines on current production vs new pipeline, and compute metrics (MRR, NDCG@10, avg rank displacement).
   - Include a 5% live A/B with safety rollback if click-through or latency deteriorates.

I've attached a first-draft runbook (lighttouch-embed-runbook-v1.pdf) that includes a proposed two-week timeline, owner matrix, and a preflight checklist. Can we schedule a 30-min sync Monday to review? Also please confirm if the May 22-23 window is still preferred.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Embeddings cutover for ACME - runbook (technical notes)

Hi all —

Following up with a technical append that expands on the runbook. I'm including throughput and safety recommendations so ACME can make an informed vendor choice. TL;DR: seed+incremental is safest for your SLA; bulk reindex is OK if you can accept a short switchover and double-write period.

Backfill & indexing notes:
- Estimated vectorize throughput on our infra: 2,500 docs/min (medium-sized doc avg) with batching and tokenization parallelism. For 500k docs that's ~200 minutes pure vectorization; plan for ~6–10 hours including I/O and shard sync.
- Sharding: prefer namespace-based sharding per tenant + time-based segments for easier rollbacks.
- Consistency: use deterministic IDs and idempotent upserts so retry doesn't create duplication.
- KV cache priming: prewarm top-K cache with heavy prefixes to reduce tail latency on day 0.

Vector DB tradeoffs (extended):
- Pinecone: great managed option; pay premium for SLA and geo-replication.
- Milvus: good performance, better control on AVX/GPUs; we recommend if ACME needs custom shard placement.
- FAISS: best when you control infra and can optimize GPU kernels; less ideal if you want rapid operational turnaround.

Rerank evaluation plan:
- Offline: 1k stratified queries, compute NDCG@10, MRR, and pairwise win-rate vs prod.
- Online: 5% A/B for 72 hours; metric gates: NDCG drop >1.5% or latency P95 > 150ms -> auto rollback.
- Smoke tests: run 200 synthetic queries post-cutover to validate latency distribution and top-1 stability.

Attachments: backfill-scripts.md (scripts and example curl upserts), throughput-estimates.csv (per-shard throughput). I'll join the Monday sync if needed.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

I sketched a concrete implementation timeline that maps to Monica/Ben's proposals. Key points:
- Prep week (May 10–14): finalize sample eval sets, spin up staging vector DB, run initial seed on 10k docs. Owners: Ben (tech run), Lauren (CS testing), ACME SRE (staging infra).
- Backfill weekend (May 22–23): bulk seed + index swap OR continuous catch-up depending on decision. We recommend running a dry-run on May 15 with a 100k subset.
- Cutover & validation (May 24–25): 72-hour A/B and smoke tests. Support on-call from Redwood for first 48 hours.

Procurement note: if ACME chooses self-hosted GPU indexers, please confirm GPU procurement by May 8; otherwise we can provision through Redwood Dedicated for limited windows.

I've attached an owner table (implementation-owners-table.csv). Monica, can you confirm final owners and whether ACME will take procurement on infra or prefer Redwood-managed? Also looping in Lauren to own ops acceptance tests.

Thanks,
